title: Build enterprise generative AI apps using Llama 3 at 1,000 tokens/s on the SambaNova AI platform

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 100%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is SambaNova's full-stack AI platform (Samba-1 CoE, SN40L RDU chip, API endpoints) as the substrate developers build generative AI applications on. SambaNova is a developer platform targeting enterprise operations, with a substantial RAG-based enterprise search exercise using embeddings, ChromaDB, and retrieval. The workshop covers building apps from notebooks (development), deploying them via SambaNova endpoints (deployment), and running inference at 1,000 tokens/second (inference_serving). The video description explicitly states 'Level: Intermediate' and requires prior Python programming experience, a GitHub account, and a laptop. The session is a hands-on workshop with two guided Jupyter notebook exercises and live demos, recorded at the AI Engineer World's Fair. Multiple transcript evidence anchors directly support the platform, inference performance, and RAG development dimensions of the classification.

summary: Michelle Matern (Director of Solutions Engineering, SambaNova) opens the workshop, introducing colleagues Petro Milan and Varun Krishna. Prerequisites include laptops, internet, Python, pip, and a Discord channel (password: TimeToBuild) for API keys. SambaNova is a full-stack AI platform founded in 2017 by Stanford professors, now in its fourth chip generation with over $1 billion in funding, targeting enterprise and government customers requiring sovereign AI at trillion-parameter scale. Samba-1 combines large monolithic and smaller fine-tuned expert models via a single secure endpoint with intelligent routing, dynamic fine-tuning scheduling, model-level RBAC, and support for direct model calling and model chaining. The pre-composed CoE includes 92 experts across seven foundation architectures, with 12 models developed or co-developed by SambaNova. Enterprise benchmarks show Samba-1 meeting or exceeding GPT 3.5 turbo and GPT 4. The SN40L RDU chip's three-tier memory (4GB SRAM, 512GB HBM, up to 6TB DDR) stores up to five trillion parameters on a single system. Petro demos Samba-1 Turbo showing Llama 3 8B at 1,000 tokens/second with 0.09s time-to-first-token. The hands-on portion begins with Exercise 1: attendees clone the repo, create a .env file with SambaNova Studio API keys, set up a Python 3.10 conda environment, and run a Jupyter notebook demonstrating LLM inference via a LangChain wrapper for SambaNova Studio. Petro shows two inference methods: direct llm.invoke() and LangChain chains with prompt templates and output parsers, noting that Llama 3 requires special tags for proper prompt formatting. Exercise 2 covers a full RAG Q&A system. Petro provides a RAG overview: document loading/parsing, splitting, vectorization using E5-large-v2 embeddings, storage in ChromaDB, retrieval via similarity metrics with optional rankers, and Q&A generation. Exercise 2 setup requires Tesseract and Poppler system packages, Python 3.10, both embedding and SambaStudio API endpoints/keys, and additional pip requirements. The notebook demo runs end-to-end: document loading via configurable data loaders (pPDF default, unstructured available), splitting the SN40L arXiv paper (15 pages) with chunk size 1200 and overlap 240 into 89 chunks, vectorization on CPU or RDU (batch size 1 or 32) taking ~4 seconds, indexing into ChromaDB, and QA chain retrieval of top K=3 chunks. Demo questions include 'What is a monolithic model?' and a table-based query about operation intensity vs. fusion level (answer: 41.4). Petro recommends switching to the unstructured data loader for complex PDF tables.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction, housekeeping, and prerequisites
sections.summary: Michelle Matern introduces herself and colleagues Petro Milan and Varun Krishna. She outlines the agenda: SambaNova overview, hands-on workshop led by Petro, and Q&A. Prerequisites include laptops, internet, Python, pip, and Discord. Attendees are guided to join a Discord channel (password: TimeToBuild) for file sharing and API keys.

sections.title: SambaNova company overview
sections.summary: SambaNova is a full-stack AI platform founded in 2017 by Stanford professors (Kunle, Chris, Rodrigo). Builds own chips (fourth generation) through system and software. Over $1 billion in funding from BlackRock, Google Ventures, Intel, GIC. Targets enterprise and government customers requiring sovereign AI at trillion-parameter scale. Integrates the full stack into a seamless experience so customers don't make individual layer decisions.

sections.title: Performance benchmarks and inference speed
sections.summary: SambaNova released a demo called One Turbo exceeding world records for Llama 3 inference speed. Artificial Analysis benchmarking showed SambaNova far exceeding other hardware providers in throughput at 1,000 tokens per second.

sections.title: Large monolithic vs. smaller expert models
sections.summary: Contrasts two paradigms: large monolithic models (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) offer broad capabilities and easy integration but have enterprise concerns around data privacy, security, per-token cost escalation, and difficulty with proprietary data. Smaller open-source models (e.g., Llama 3 8B) enable fine-tuning for enterprise accuracy, security, and data ownership, but create manageability challenges with many micro-models to orchestrate and fine-tune.

sections.title: Samba-1 core capabilities: single endpoint and routing
sections.summary: Samba-1 combines the best of both paradigms. Four core capabilities are introduced, two covered here: (1) all fine-tuned expert models sit behind a single secure endpoint; (2) a router determines the best expert for each incoming prompt.

sections.title: Samba-1 core capabilities: fine-tuning scheduling and RBAC; CoE composition
sections.summary: Two additional Samba-1 capabilities are detailed: dynamic fine-tuning scheduling (different cadences per expert, e.g., finance annually, coding quarterly) and model-level RBAC for fine-grained access control by application, person, or group. Samba-1 offers a flexible CoE (custom model selection) and a pre-composed CoE with 92 experts covering broad languages, domains, and enterprise tasks across seven foundation architectures (Llama 2, Llama 3, Mistral, Falcon, Bloom, plus multimodal: Lava, Clip, DeepPlot). SambaNova developed or co-developed 12 of the 92 models, including Thai, Japanese, and Hungarian language models, a text-to-SQL model, and contributions to BLOOMChat.

sections.title: Enterprise benchmarking and orchestration capabilities
sections.summary: SambaNova created an enterprise-grade AI benchmarking suite measuring against GPT 3.5 turbo and GPT 4 across tasks like information extraction, text-to-SQL, coding, and function calling, meeting or exceeding OpenAI capabilities. Beyond routing, the product supports direct model calling and model chaining for agentic AI workflows.

sections.title: SN40L RDU chip and three-tier memory architecture
sections.summary: SambaNova's chip is called an RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit), current version SN40L. Its unique three-tier memory architecture includes 4GB on-chip SRAM, 512GB HBM, and up to 6TB DDR, storing up to five trillion parameters on a single chip. Models move up the memory stack for execution. Unlike GPUs, which require multiple systems to host many models, SambaNova stores a huge number of models on one system.

sections.title: Samba-1 Turbo live demo
sections.summary: Petro demos Samba-1 Turbo on sambanova.ai, selecting Llama 3 8B and asking it to create a three-day workout schedule. The demo shows 1,000 tokens/second throughput, 0.09s time-to-first-token, and 0.65s total inference time. A comparison with ChatGPT on the same prompt shows a visible speed difference. A real-time chat mode is also demonstrated, where the model responds instantly as the user types.

sections.title: Hands-on workshop introduction and Exercise 1 setup
sections.summary: Petro introduces two hands-on exercises. Exercise 1 is a basic example: loading environment variables, setting up the SambaNova API, initializing the LLM, and making a simple inference call in Python. Exercise 2 is a practical RAG Q&A system for enterprise search using LangChain, data loaders, E5-large-v2 embeddings, ChromaDB vector store, and Llama 3 8B Instruct. Attendees are directed to the GitHub repo (ai-starter-kit, workshops/ai_engineer_2024/basic_examples), instructed to clone the repo and create a .env file with the SambaNova Studio API key.

sections.title: Exercise 1 setup and demo: basic LLM inference
sections.summary: Petro walks through Exercise 1 setup: creating a .env file with SambaNova Studio API keys (available on Discord), creating a Python 3.10 conda environment, installing requirements via pip, and linking the Jupyter kernel. The demo covers loading libraries (LangChain wrapper for SambaNova Studio), loading environment variables, initializing the LLM with model configs (do_sample for deterministic vs. probabilistic output, temperature, max_tokens), and setting the expert to Meta Llama 3 8B Instruct. Petro demonstrates two inference methods: llm.invoke() with a direct prompt, and LangChain chains combining prompt templates, LLM, and output parsers. He notes that open-source models like Llama 3 require special tags/tokens (from the meta model card) to properly delineate the beginning of text, user query, and answer boundaries; without these tags, the model produces extraneous output.

sections.title: RAG overview and Exercise 2 introduction
sections.summary: Petro transitions to Exercise 2, a Q&A system with RAG. He provides a RAG overview: RAG supplements LLMs with additional information from various sources to improve responses, useful for querying beyond training data, accessing up-to-date information without retraining, and reducing hallucinations. The typical RAG workflow consists of: (1) document loading and parsing using data loaders for PDF, text, PowerPoint; (2) splitting into smaller chunks with chunk size and overlap as hyperparameters; (3) vectorization using E5-large-v2 to map chunks to numerical vectors; (4) storage in a vector store like ChromaDB; (5) retrieval using similarity metrics with optional ranker for relevance filtering; (6) Q&A generation providing the LLM with the query and retrieved chunks for grounded response. Third-party tools handle loading, splitting, and storage; embeddings can run on CPU or SambaNova hardware; the LLM runs on SambaNova hardware.

sections.title: Exercise 2 setup: dependencies and environment
sections.summary: Petro walks through Exercise 2 setup. The .env file (at the ai-starter-kit level) requires both embedding endpoint/key and SambaStudio endpoint/key, available on Discord. System packages include Tesseract (OCR, via brew install tesseract) and Poppler (brew install poppler). A Python 3.10 virtual environment is recommended (install via command if needed, add path to shell config). The installation script takes approximately 5 minutes. Additional fixes may be needed for nltk and SSL certificates on some laptops. IPyKernel must be installed and the kernel linked to the notebook. The exercise provides both a Jupyter notebook (rag_langchain_llama3_1b) and a Streamlit app. The notebook imports shared modules including document_retrieval and vector DB utilities.

sections.title: Exercise 2 demo: RAG Q&A system execution
sections.summary: Petro runs the Exercise 2 notebook end-to-end. Document loading uses configurable data loaders (pPDF default, unstructured available via config file). The SN40L arXiv paper (15 pages) serves as the test document, placed under data/temp. LangChain's recursive splitter divides the paper into 89 chunks with chunk size 1200 and overlap 240. Vectorization uses the E5-large-v2 embedding model, runnable on CPU or RDU (SambaStudio endpoint, batch size 1 or 32, CoE set to false for standalone), taking approximately 4 seconds. Embeddings are indexed into ChromaDB. The QA chain embeds queries, retrieves top K=3 chunks (no ranker used), and passes question plus context to the LLM for grounded answers. Demo questions include 'What is a monolithic model?' (instantaneous response) and a table-based question about operation intensity vs. fusion level (answer: 41.4). Petro recommends switching to the unstructured data loader for more complex PDF tables, configurable via the config file.
